# Cloudflare Workers Free candidate — 2026-09-26

**Disposition:** provisional interface candidate, not a qualified default or production release. A dedicated Cloudflare token now exists; no provider inference has been sent.

The owner’s existing Cloudflare account was already signed in. The dashboard showed **Workers Free** active and a separate **R2 Paid** subscription. R2 is outside the campaign. After specific action-time approval, a 30-day account token named `Co-Scientist free campaign` was created with only Workers AI Read and Write. The account list showed that exact scope, and the token verification API returned HTTP 200, `active`, with expiry 2026-10-26 23:59:59 UTC. Its value is held only in an owner-readable local file outside the repository; the file is mode 600. Do not use the R2 token or broaden the campaign token's scope.

[Cloudflare pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/) gives Workers Free 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge and says over-limit operations fail. Usage above that allocation requires Workers Paid; merely having a separate R2 Paid subscription does not establish a Workers Paid plan. The listed [`@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` model](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/%40cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it/) has 256,000-token context, function calling and streaming. It is not in Cloudflare’s [documented JSON Mode model list](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/json-mode/), so the project’s JSON boundary is an empirical question. [Cloudflare’s data-use policy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/data-usage/) says Workers AI content is not used to train models or improve services or shared with other customers; it is not a blanket zero-retention guarantee.

The test-first provisional guard admits only the exact Gemma model, an account-pinned OpenAI-compatible endpoint, an operator attestation bound to the current UTC date and Workers Free plan, and a dedicated token. It excludes SDK fallback/alias routing, paid-model substitution, server tools and unrecognized options. It sends `options.rejectIfBusy: true` to fail fast under capacity pressure. It accepts only the engine’s bounded `json_object` and `json_schema` request shapes for **qualification**, without claiming the provider supports either. It forces LiteLLM’s `drop_params` off so an unsupported JSON parameter produces an observable error instead of silently becoming a prompt-only response. A 4,096-token output cap limits exploratory requests and deliberately rejects the engine’s 24,000-token output case. The attestation is an assertion, not an automated plan or quota readback; it is unsuitable as an unattended production control without further design.

The public `call_llm` and `call_llm_json` boundaries were exercised with mocked transport, including streaming/tool arguments, both JSON request formats and a real project schema envelope with `strict: false`. The first red test reproduced the original OpenRouter-only rejection; a subsequent red test showed the JSON call could not reach the provider until the guard admitted its exact shape. Final focused engine tests: 102 passed; adjacent app free-request tests: 23 passed; Ruff, mypy and `git diff --check` passed. No live compatibility, served-model, scientific-quality, billing or full-run evidence exists. M11-OPS-02c and its dependent items stay open.

## Bounded next check

The [model page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/%40cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it/) lists `response_format` and `max_completion_tokens` in a generic API schema, without a model-specific guarantee for JSON compliance or a 24,000-token output ceiling. Before any call, recheck Workers Free, remaining daily Neurons, model eligibility, data use and exact token scope; pin the code and fixed public-input hashes. Then use one exact configuration through the project interfaces, with no paid fallback or retries: first one `call_llm_json` schema case, then only on success a tool round trip capped at two physical requests, one streaming case, and one long-input/output-budget case after a test-first adjustment to the provisional 4,096-token guard. Stop at the first timeout, rate limit, unsupported parameter, missing served-model/usage receipt or wrong route. Do not repeat an unresponsive case. Only if every interface case passes should the retained four-claim batch gate run, stopping on the first completed wrong-label trial and requiring three passing fresh trials before broader selection. A pass here would still require the rest of M11-OPS-02c's full-run, privacy, zero-spend and release evidence. The token creation and bounded public-input trial are authorized; this procedure does not establish model qualification or an unattended production configuration.

The [official error table](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/errors/) distinguishes Free allocation exhaustion (`3036`, HTTP 429), temporary capacity (`3040`, HTTP 429, including `rejectIfBusy`), and a model that requires Workers Paid (`5035`, HTTP 403). Retain the exact provider code. A `3036` is a quota stop until the next 00:00 UTC reset, `3040` fails the present route reliability check without repeated probes, and `5035` disqualifies the model under zero additional spending. No paid-plan upgrade or alternative billing path is authorized.

For an unattended default, the dated operator attestation is still unresolved. Cloudflare's [subscription read API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/accounts/subresources/subscriptions/methods/get/) requires `Billing Read` or `Billing Write`, neither included in the draft Workers AI-only token. Granting either would be a separate security-scope decision; do not assume the current draft can automatically verify Workers Free each day. [AI Gateway ZDR](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/unified-billing/) applies only to Unified Billing with Cloudflare-managed credentials, which requires purchased credits, and does not control gateway logging. [Gateway spend limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/spend-limits/) are estimate-based and eventually consistent, so they cannot prove zero additional spending. Keep direct Workers AI for bounded public-input qualification; do not add a gateway as a privacy or billing workaround.

An independent Antigravity Gemini 3.8 Flash High diff review found a misspelled test environment variable and the original JSON-blocking gap; both were corrected. Its claim that Workers Free automatically bills overage was contradicted by the current Cloudflare pricing page and was not adopted. The review also highlighted the dated attestation and BYOK interaction; campaign mode intentionally overrides BYOK under the existing policy, while explicit BYOK outside campaign mode remains unchanged.
